#54458. Breaking: How to Blind-Bake Pie Crust—and When You Need To

📅 16 May 2016 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1446 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Bonappetit ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: How to Blind-Bake Pie Crust—and When You Need To

📅 16 May 2016 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1446 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bonappetit

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the road to pie perfection is paved in pitfalls.
  • But getting the crust to the right color depends on what you’re planning to fill it with.
  • Blind baking is especially useful when the filling needs less time in the oven than the crust does.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the road to pie perfection is paved in pitfalls. I’ve fallen into plenty of them throughout my baking career. The infamous “soggy bottom” is among the most common, but it’s easy to avoid. Blind baking—baking the crust before adding the filling—helps prevent an underbaked crust by giving the pastry a head start in the oven or cooking it completely before the filling goes in.

But getting the crust to the right color depends on what you’re planning to fill it with. A pale, partially baked shell might be perfect for one pie, while another needs a deep golden brown crust before you add even a spoonful of filling. Here’s how to know when enough color is enough.

Blind baking is especially useful when the filling needs less time in the oven than the crust does. For custard pies, like pumpkin pie, partially baking the shell gives the pastry a head start so it doesn’t end up uncooked beneath a set filling. For pies with no-bake fillings, such as chocolate pudding pie or cranberry curd pie, the crust needs to be fully baked before it’s filled.

Sources indicate that most traditional fruit pies don’t need blind baking. Their fillings and crusts spend enough time in the oven together for the pastry to cook through. There are exceptions, particularly single-crust fruit pies topped with a crumble. Our Peach-Blueberry Pie, for example, starts with a thoroughly blind-baked shell before the filling goes in. Follow your recipe’s instructions rather than assuming every fruit pie needs the same treatment.

According to recent reports, start with a good pie dough. Roll it out, fit it into the pie plate, and crimp the edge. Chill the shaped shell for at least 15 minutes before baking; cold dough holds its shape better in the oven, reducing the risk of shrinking or slumping.

In a recent development, next, line the shell with parchment paper and fill it with pie weights. Crumpling the parchment first, then unfolding it, helps it conform to the shell. The weights hold the dough against the pan while it bakes, preventing the bottom from puffing up and the sides from collapsing.

Sources indicate that you can buy ceramic pie weights or use dried beans, rice, or stainless-steel ball bearings. I’m partial to the ball bearings: They’re small enough to settle into the corners of the pie plate and heavy enough to hold the dough firmly in place.

Not everyone in the Bon Appétit Test Kitchen agrees. Editors Jesse Szewczyk and Rebecca Firkser prefer lighter alternatives. In their experience, heavy metal weights can compress the dough, limiting the expansion of the buttery layers that make pie crust flaky. Jesse uses dried beans or rice; Rebecca prefers dried chickpeas or even granulated sugar, a technique popularized by baking expert Stella Parks.

All of these options can work. Whichever you choose, fill the parchment-lined shell generously, supporting the sides all the way to the rim. Leave the weights in place until the crust looks dry and set and the parchment releases easily; removing them too soon can cause the sides to slump.

Our Cranberry Meringue Pie has a fully blind-baked pie crust.

It has been revealed that this method uses our Perfect Pie Crust dough and makes one 9"-diameter pie shell. It produces an evenly golden crust; if your pie calls for a paler or more deeply browned shell, follow its specific baking instructions and use the visual guide below.

Some pie recipes call for docking (pricking the bottom and sides of the dough with a fork) before baking. This allows steam to escape and helps prevent uneven puffing, but doesn’t replace the support of pie weights. Follow your recipe’s instructions; docking isn’t necessary for every blind-baked crust.

According to recent reports, do Ahead: A fully blind-baked crust can be made up to 2 days ahead. Let cool completely, wrap well, and store at room temperature until ready to fill.

The short answer: It depends on what you’re putting inside. Some pies need only a partially baked crust, while others call for a shell that’s deeply golden brown.

It has been revealed that oven temperatures vary, different pie plates conduct heat differently, and the filling determines how much additional baking the crust will get. Use the recipe’s timing as a guide, but watch the color and texture of the pastry. Here’s what to look for.

Industry observers note that fruit pies need a pale base because they bake a looong time. Or at least, that’s often the thinking. If you’re making a single-crust variety topped with a crumble, such as our Blueberry Crumble Pie, and the recipe calls for blind-baking, you might want to start with an anemic crust. It’ll have plenty of time to brown as the juices thicken.

Recent findings suggest that A pale, partially baked crust should look set rather than raw. The bottom should look set and opaque with some light golden patches, while the crimped edge may already be noticeably browned. The crust will continue to develop color once the filling goes in.

Don’t assume fruit pies always need a pale shell. Our Peach-Blueberry Pie, for example, calls for a well-browned crust before the fruit and crumble go in. And many double-crust fruit pies don’t need blind baking at all.

A lightly baked shell can also be appropriate for custards that have a substantial bake ahead. BA’s Best Pumpkin Pie starts with a partially baked crust before the custard goes in for at least another hour.

The goal is to give the crust enough of a head start without taking it so far that the edges burn before the filling finishes cooking.

Custard pies, such as chess and our Lemon Buttermilk Pie, often have shorter bake times than fruit pies, so the crust needs a solid golden base layer to develop enough color by the time the filling sets.

Here, you’re looking for more than a crust that’s simply dry and set. The bottom should be evenly golden with no pale, translucent patches, and the sides should have taken on some color too. The rim will generally be a little darker than the bottom, but the whole shell should look well on its way to being fully baked.

In a recent development, our Perfect Pie Crust recipe produces this kind of shell. It calls for baking the weighted crust until the edges are golden, then removing the weights and continuing until the bottom and sides are evenly browned.

Recent findings suggest that and some pies need an even more substantial head start. Our Bourbon-Date Pecan Pie takes the crust to a dry golden finish before adding a filling that bakes for another 45–55 minutes.

The point isn’t that every custard pie needs the same color. It’s that the crust should be baked far enough that it won’t be left pale and doughy by the time the filling is done.

Recent findings suggest that bake the crust to a dark golden brown if you’re adding a no-bake filling, like a pudding or curd. You’re going for a toasty, burnished color, so don’t be gun-shy.

Because the filling won’t return to the oven, this is the crust’s one chance to bake all the way through. You want deep color across the entire bottom and up the sides—not just a dark rim surrounding a pale center. The pastry should look dry, crisp, and well browned, without any doughy or translucent spots.

According to recent reports, after removing the pie weights, continue baking until the shell is fully browned, checking frequently toward the end. Depending on the dough and oven temperature, that might take another 15–20 minutes or longer. Don’t pull it simply because the timer has gone off.

Sources indicate that our Cranberry Meringue Pie uses this approach: The crust is baked until golden and dry before the cranberry curd filling goes in. A fully baked shell develops a richer, toastier flavor and is better equipped to stand up to a moist filling.

Some recipes, including our pumpkin pie, call for brushing a thin layer of beaten egg onto the partially baked shell and returning it to the oven briefly to set. This, ostensibly, creates a barrier between the pastry and the filling, but not all bakers believe the hype.

Industry observers note that while it can be a useful extra precaution, it is by no means a universal requirement. If your recipe doesn’t call for it, there’s no need to add another step.

They’ll be here whenever you need them.

  • If you’re one of the many fans who’ve cleared out their schedule to binge the game this weekend, you’ll want to make sure you emerge from your haze with extremities that still function.
  • “The metaphor we like to share with pro players or casual gamers is the concept of the health bar,” indicates Dr.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the day has finally arrived. Grand Theft Auto VI is here, and you’ve taken that “sick day” to cause chaos on the streets of Vice City. After more than 10 years of waiting, you’re finally back in one of the franchise’s most classic locations, this time with an open world to explore. It’s not hyperbole to call this the most highly anticipated game in history. With more than 17 million preorders, that’s a lot of people who will be running from the police while trying to avoid (or rack up) six stars.

If you’re one of the many fans who’ve cleared out their schedule to binge the game this weekend, you’ll want to make sure you emerge from your haze with extremities that still function.

“The metaphor we like to share with pro players or casual gamers is the concept of the health bar,” indicates Dr. Matthew Hwu, owner of physical therapy clinic 1 Health Point in Monrovia, California. “The muscles and tendons of your wrist, hand, thumb, as you move the analog stick, only have so much capacity or ‘max HP’ that they can handle throughout the day.”.

It has been revealed that below, we spoke with Dr. Hwu and other veteran gamers about how to keep your “HP” bar full for your whole weekend without developing carpal tunnel.

Recent findings suggest that playing a game for long hours puts the soft tissues in your hands and arms into overdrive. When you ramp things up, you’ll feel sore and fatigued. The most common version of this is “tendon-based problems of the wrist and hand,” says Dr. Hwu, who has spent more than 11 years working with e-sports players to help them recover from injuries. As GTA VI will be available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S and X, most people will be using a controller, which puts the thumbs under a lot of stress as people “control the analog stick to flip left, up, right, down; press A, B, X, Y.” The most common gaming injuries are gamer’s thumb and tennis elbow, according to the Cleveland Clinic.

It has been revealed that so, don’t forget to take breaks. Dr. Hwu recommends at least a five-minute break for every 90 minutes played, though younger players are more resilient. If you want to push it, the key is taking longer breaks afterwards. “Two hours, 10-minute break, three hours, 15-minute break,” Dr. Hwu says. “If you want to be degenerate, you can be a smart degen.” You can also be strategic about scheduling more downtime after sequences with higher APM (actions per minute), that are more intensive on hand muscles. In essence, go touch grass after a high-stakes bank robbery.

That noted, after more than a decade of waiting for what our reviewer described as “the most technically and artistically impressive game world ever made,” your instinct may be to lock in. So it’s wise to plan for breaks ahead of time. Set alarms on your phone or watch. If one goes off in the middle of a mission, commit to taking a break after crashing that helicopter. Make sure you eat and stay hydrated, and move your body, whether that’s a neighborhood walk or just a short twirl around your apartment before your next mission.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s basically just your muscle and tendon tissue recovery, it’ll restore a little bit of HP over time,” Dr. Hwu says. “When you go out and walk outdoors, that can help with your overall circulation, nervous system as well. So you don’t feel like that meme where you come out of the cave and you’re like a ghost.”.

Just like in other forms of training, stretching is a key part of your self-care arsenal for long hours of gaming. To loosen up for a long stretch of car-hijacking, do a few stretches before turning on your console, and during cut scenes. Your body will tell you what areas feel tight and could use some attention. But don’t forget those thumb muscles. “Bring your thumb away from the next finger, stretching it down,” Dr. Hwu says. “Every time you’re flicking back, left, or right, you might be using these muscles.”.

It has been revealed that you’ll also want to stretch your index fingers after long hours of beating ass with a crowbar while riding your motorcycle. “Every time you press your trigger,” Dr. Hwu says, “you’re using the extensors, the top side of your fingers, but also the flexors to push down.” You can also work on relaxing your forearm muscles, by extending your arm out and pushing your palm downward.

It has been revealed that after 13 years, and a budget rumored to rival that of Dubai’s Burj Khalifa skyscraper, the new Grand Theft Auto is finally here. Our critic's verdict? It's a tour de force that reimagines what a video game can be.

It has been revealed that don’t forget your neck and upper back, which can feel stiff from holding onto stress after high speed chases and parachute combat. It’s so easy to load tension onto those upper traps as you shrimp further into your recliner while bird watching, or scoring a pair of black half-rim sunglasses and Eris sneakers (definitely not Nikes) for Jason (no judgment here).

Recent findings suggest that “I will do small things: roll my neck from side to side, stretch my traps by sitting on one hand and pulling my head [in the] opposite direction,” Calliope Ryder, platform director at GYLD, previously a producer on Tales of the Shire, says. “[I] tense my calves in spurts to help with blood flow, or stand up and let my body fold at the hips while swaying side to side with my arms crossed. Again, alerts to remind me to do it are necessary or I'll go hours without noticing.”.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, using a heating pad or an ice pack on a sore area (like your lower back) can help with any nagging dull pain you’re feeling. Heat loosens up stiff muscles, while ice can help dull the achy sensation. They won’t build your long-term strength, but they’ll make you feel better in the moment.

If you’re old enough for back pain, then you’re old enough to have to consider video game ergonomics. Wherever you’re gaming, Dr. Hwu’s recommendation is simple: Sit with your legs at a 90-degree angle, feet planted on the ground, back appropriately supported. Then put a pillow on your lap and rest your arms on it. This helps prevent forearm strain and hunching over. You can even haul your expensive Aeron from your office into the living room, rather than rotting on the sofa and ruining your back.

It has been revealed that there are also a number of helpful gaming peripherals. Maddy Myers, editor in chief and co-founder of video game publication Mothership, uses a specific gaming pillow from a brand called Mechanism. “The pillow allows you to have the handheld device suspended in the air in a comfortable, adjustable spot so that you don’t tire out your arms from holding it up,” she claims. “You can also put a controller on there.”.

Using the device helps her get through play stretches of eight hours a day on the weekends, “while taking breaks to eat, do chores, stretch.” It’s been especially invaluable during high-intensity work periods. “I have to play GTA 6 for my job, so I am really going to be relying on these tools to keep my arms and body feeling as close to normal as possible,” she says.

Don’t let a terribly designed controller be the reason you develop carpal tunnel. Julia Lee, section lead for video game guides at Polygon, plays at least two hours of games a day, and will sometimes fit in 10-hour sessions. Her wrists started hurting and “those flat [Nintendo Switch] Joy-Cons were directly to blame,” she states. “I ended up getting a Nintendo Switch Pro Controller (which has a much more ergonomic shape and grip), and that helped alleviate pain a lot.” She also reminds herself not to hold the controller so tight, as it causes pain.

As Dr. Hwu explains, some controllers have staggered sticks, while others have an inline design. It all comes down to individual comfort and muscular endurance. He’s helped pro Call of Duty players modify their analog sticks, and has coached people to avoid death-gripping the controller. “If you use a claw grip position, an awkward grip, or a modded controller, that might lead to more stress for certain muscles in your wrist and hand,” he indicates.

According to recent reports, if your hands are really killing you, there’s also the option of switching to another controller style altogether. “Moving two to four of my most awkward hand-based actions from my hands to my feet allows me to play longer,” John Warren, chief marketing officer and cofounder of Glydr, a foot-based video game controller, indicates. Warren has minicore disease, which causes muscle weakness. “Anytime you have an opportunity to stop overloading your hands while you play, you give your hands a little reprieve,” he says, “it makes your high-precision hand actions more accurate.”.

Lastly, if you have existing injuries, and your medical provider has prescribed a brace, actually follow their guidance for how and when to use it. For my part, I use thumb braces called the Push Metagrips, to help support my floppy thumb joints anytime I blueprint on playing video games for long stretches.

So you’ve done all this work to binge GTA 6, and you’re feeling solid but a little sore. But you want to play for longer periods, snipe with greater accuracy, and fuck around with less fatigue. Consider going to the gym.

Recent findings suggest that doing exercises for those small muscles and tendons can help you build up that tolerance, like any other form of weight and endurance training. “When you rest, ice, massage, kinesio tape, you know, passive interventions, bracing, all of these things can restore your HP,” Dr. Hwu notes. “It does nothing to change the size of your health bar, which represents the tissue’s capacity or your endurance. The way we do that is you can do specific exercises to build up or create a buffer for how much you’re going to handle.”.

For any chronic pain, injuries, or conditions, it’s notable to work with a physical therapist. I’m currently working with one for repetitive stress injury recovery, and doing exercises specific to playing video games. I do slow wrist curls with a two-pound weight, rotator cuff exercises with a resistance band, and squeeze an egg-shaped stress ball for thumb and forearm endurance. I also train my shoulders and core.

For those who aren’t managing any injuries, training those finger and arm muscles make it easier to game for longer periods. Consistency is key, and so is having reasonable expectations. Dr. Hwu recommends starting once a day, three to four times a week, “on a day where you’re not doing a lot, and then you’ll learn how your body responds to doing exercises within the context of your specific life, and you can make modifications to scale up the aggressiveness or scale down,” he notes. As for seeing progress, “it takes four to six weeks for muscles, eight weeks for tendons.”.

In a recent development, and don’t forget the stabilizer muscles in your shoulders, which hold up your upper body and support your arms. “I focus on ‘chest opening’ exercises that strengthen your back,” Ryder says. “I tend towards curving forward so I consciously strengthen the 'opposite' muscles so they pull my shoulders back a bit.” She also does chin tucks, to strengthen her deep neck flexors.

Industry observers note that strength training is also a great way to tackle back pain, another common complaint after gaming for hours. “A few years ago I started having extreme back pain when I sat in my office chair,” Gita Jackson, cofounder of video game publication Aftermath, claims. They play one to two hours of games a day, but often play marathon sessions when new games come out. “The pain was excruciating, and sometimes my legs would get so stiff I couldn’t walk. Recovery started with physical therapy, and then a new ergonomic chair,” and now they regularly attend pilates.

“I really had no idea that if I wanted to continue playing noodley strategy games without pain that I would have to be a person who works out multiple times a week,” they say.

In a recent development, maybe you’ve done a little too much, and your arms start to feel heavy as bricks, with thumbs that ache for hours. Even with the best precautions in place, it can happen to any of us.

According to recent reports, “If it gets to a point where cumulatively, over days, symptoms are getting worse, maybe reflect and identify what you could change,” Dr. Hwu claims. “If things are consistently sharp, or you start to feel some weakness, where when you go and try to pick up something, you’ll want to drop it. That’s a sign that it may be time to make a change in some of the variables that you can control.”.

In 2002, weeks before the release of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, the journalist David Kushner met Sam and Dan Houser, plus Rockstar co-founder Terry Donovan, at their SoHo loft. It would be their last and only in-depth sit-down before they decided that the world’s most successful video game required little explanation.

This is when paying attention to your daily habits is key. Instead of freaking out over hand pain, and deciding you need to quit playing cold turkey, you can instead think about what you did during the day that might have contributed to your discomfort. “How much you’re playing, what intensity you’re playing, are you taking breaks, are you exercising, how are you responding to the pain?” Dr. Hwu states. These are all factors in why you might be having pain, and all things to consider modifying. If it truly is tendon fatigue, then the key is finding the right volume of use, rather than quitting altogether.

According to recent reports, there are also some signs to look out for that may require medical intervention. Dr. Hwu pointed me to 1 Health Point’s website, which suggests seeking a doctor’s opinion if your wrist looks swollen or bruised, if you can’t move or bear any weight, if your symptoms worsen or spread with rest, or if you experience constant hand numbness, especially if it comes with weakness.

Gaming for long hours ultimately comes down to using your common sense alongside your precious free will. Pay attention to your habits. Commit to taking breaks and stretching between bank robberies and doomscrolling through Snapmatic (in-game social media). Do some preventative exercises while planning out your next mission—with a soundtrack that includes Bad Bunny and Dua Lipa, as well as some ’80s bangers, you’ve already got the music for it. Your hands and arms will thank you, even if the regular people of Leonida probably won’t.

Industry observers note that more recently, some of Schafer’s most noteworthy style moments have included her gauzy pink 2024 Golden Globes dress by Prada. “The organza was super long—it was essentially a train—and it so happened to be a very windy day,” recalls Schafer. “The wind picked up all the organza, and floated around me. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, traditionally, cornbread stuffing requires making cornbread, cubing it and letting it dry out, mixing it with stock, eggs, meat, and aromatics, then transforming it into a stuffing (or dressing). This process produces some truly memorable casseroles, but I have an alternative that streamlines the process without compromising flavor: stuffing cornbread. It still smells enticingly like the classic Thanksgiving side as you set the baking dish on the table. I’ve still packed in a medley of woodsy herbs, sweet onions, vegetal peppers, and savory sausage. And it still slices into lofty servings to perch on your plate next to the sweet potatoes and green beans. It just takes half as long to make.

The intentional two-to-one ratio of cornmeal to flour in this cornbread results in a moist, tender crumb that still has enough structure to hold up against the sturdy mix-ins. The sugar might seem like a lot, but it balances out the savory sausage and aromatics perfectly.

For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.

It has been revealed that place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 400°. Line a 13x9" baking pan with parchment paper, leaving generous overhang on long sides. Coat pan and parchment with unsalted butter. Melt ½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium-low heat, then pour into a small bowl.

Cook 1 green bell pepper, halved, ribs and seeds removed, finely chopped, 1 medium white onion, finely chopped, and 2 celery stalks, finely chopped, in same skillet, stirring occasionally with a wooden spoon, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add 1 lb. spicy and/or sweet Italian sausage, casings removed, and cook, breaking up and stirring occasionally, until browned (it may still be a little raw in the center at this point), about 5 minutes. Remove from heat.

According to recent reports, stir together 4 cups (624 g) fine-ground yellow cornmeal, 2 cups (250 g) all-purpose flour, 1 cup (200 g) sugar, 1 Tbsp. plus 1½ tsp. baking powder, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 tsp. baking soda, and ¼ cup finely chopped sage, thyme, and/or rosemary in a large bowl. Gradually pour in 3½ cups buttermilk, then melted butter, stirring constantly until combined. Add 4 large eggs one at a time, mixing to incorporate after each addition. Fold in sausage mixture, then scrape batter into prepared pan.

It has been revealed that bake cornbread, rotating pan front to back halfway through, until golden brown and top springs back when gently pressed, 38–45 minutes. Let cool in pan 15 minutes. Using parchment paper overhang, lift cornbread out of pan and transfer to a cutting board. Cut into 12–18 slices; arrange on a platter.

In a recent development, do Ahead: Cornbread can be baked 4 hours ahead. Store at room temperature; cut just before serving.

Sources indicate that if you've spent any time on food TikTok, you've probably come across Glace's famous S'mores Hot Chocolate. The New York City dessert shop has become a social media sensation thanks to its ridiculously rich hot chocolate, complete with a thick ring of toasted marshmallow fluff around the cup and hefty scoop of whipped cream to top it off. And now you won't have to book a trip to Manhattan and stand in line just to try it.

Glace has officially rolled out its first-ever at-home hot chocolate mix, giving fans across the country the opportunity to recreate its signature drink without leaving their kitchens. And given how popular the in-store sensation has become, I'm guessing plenty of people will add this easy-to-duplicate version to their holiday wish lists.

Founded by Sasha Zabar in 2023, Glace first opened on Upcoming York City's Upper East Side, where its over-the-top S'mores Hot Chocolate swiftly became the star of the menu. The drink, which features rich drinking chocolate surrounded by a toasted marshmallow rim, has attracted plenty of attention online.

Since then, the brand has continued to dominate social media with other over-the-top menu items like its à la mode Warm Brownie Pudding Cake and Matcha Fudge Sundae, and has also expanded with a seasonal holiday truck at Rockefeller Center and Glace Candy, a neighboring shop specializing in gummies, chocolates, and other sweets.

But its newest launch means you don't have to live anywhere near New York to get a taste of at least one of its viral treats.

The upcoming Signature Hot Chocolate Mix costs $19.99 and comes with six individual sachets, each containing the same hot chocolate recipe served at Glace's shops.

Recent findings suggest that according to the brand, the mix is made with ground chocolate and A2 milk powder, without the cornstarch or powdered fillers commonly used in conventional hot chocolate mixes. The result is designed to deliver the same rich, glossy consistency that made the drink famous.

Preparing it is pretty straightforward: Simply whisk the mix over medium-low heat on the stovetop until it transforms into a thick, decadent drinking chocolate. Sadly, the at-home version doesn’t come with the shop’s signature marshmallow rim...at least, not yet.

In a recent development, glace says it's planning to release its signature marshmallow fluff separately, allowing customers to eventually recreate the full experience at home, toasted marshmallow rim and all. The brand hasn't revealed an official release date for the fluff, but we're keeping an eye out.

For now, the hot chocolate mix is available for pre-order on Glace's website, with shipments expected to begin in early December.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recipe by Taste of Home Test Kitchen.

Tested by Taste of Home Test Kitchen.

Taste of Home's Editorial Process.

Industry observers note that this cranberry Brie pull-apart bread recipe is bursting with melted cheese and sweet-savory cranberry butter. It's an interactive joy to eat.

Industry observers note that I may be a year-round cranberry fan, but it’s hard to deny just how right it feels to feast on the ruby-colored fruit during the holiday season. Fresh and frozen cranberries are perfect for cranberry sauce and not-too-sweet cranberry desserts, but I also love using dried cranberries in everything from muffins to party appetizers. And my newly introduced favorite way to use dried cranberries is in cranberry Brie pull-apart bread, where they transform a loaf of cheesy bread into a holiday masterpiece.

It has been revealed that cranberry Brie pull-apart bread is what happens when you make a mashup of party cheese bread and cranberry butter. A crusty, round loaf of sourdough is cut in a grid pattern and stuffed with half a pound of cubed Brie. The cheese-stuffed loaf is then coated in a dried cranberry-honey butter (bolstered by orange zest, garlic and rosemary) and baked until it’s hot, crispy and melty. It’s hearty, decadent, sweet, salty and impossible to stop eating.

Preheat the oven to 350°F. In a small bowl, beat together the softened butter, finely chopped dried cranberries, honey, grated orange zest, minced garlic and salt until they’re blended.

Cut the bread into 1-inch slices to within 1/2 inch of the bottom of the loaf. Repeat cuts in the opposite direction. Insert the cubed Brie into the cuts.

In a recent development, editor’s Tip: If your sourdough is crusty, a serrated bread knife will get the job done without too much elbow grease. The best bread knives slice cleanly without tearing the fluffy interior.

Spread the cranberry butter over the top of the bread. Wrap the loaf in foil and place it on a baking sheet.

Sources indicate that bake the bread for 20 minutes. Unwrap it and continue to bake it until the cheese is melted, about 10 minutes longer. If desired, drizzle it with hot honey before serving it.

Ellie Crowley For Taste Of Home.

Sources indicate that wrap leftover cranberry Brie pull-apart bread tightly, or transfer it to a food storage bag and refrigerate it for up to four days. To reheat it, wrap the bread in foil and bake it at 350º until it’s warm. Unwrap it and continue to bake until the cheese is melted and the bread is crisp. If the bread got pulled apart enough that it’s not really holding its shape anymore, transfer it to a baking dish, bake it until it’s melty, and eat it like stuffing.

Cranberry Brie pull-apart bread tastes best hot and crispy right out of the oven, but you can assemble the bread a few hours ahead of time, wrap it in foil, and refrigerate it until it’s ready to bake. You can also make and refrigerate the cranberry butter up to four days in advance and soften it at room temperature before using it. If you want to bring it to a party or Friendsgiving, follow good party etiquette and check with the host about whether the oven will be available to bake it when you arrive.

Ellie Crowley For Taste Of Home.

If your pull-apart bread is soggy, it might need to be baked longer or at a slightly higher temperature—especially if your bread is really fresh and soft. I use kitchen timers and oven thermometers to track my bakes and ensure my oven isn’t running cooler or hotter than I’d like. Don’t be afraid to bake the bread for a little longer than the recipe suggests if it hasn’t crisped on the outside or if the cheese isn’t fully melted.

According to recent reports, sourdough’s structure (and slightly sharp flavor) is perfect against the richness of the Brie and cranberry butter, but if sourdough isn’t for you, try a round, crusty loaf of rustic white bread. Get a loaf that weighs about 1 pound. Whole wheat and multigrain loaves can work as well, but they tend to have a denser texture and tighter crumb that won’t pull apart as easily. If you can’t find a round loaf, an oval-shaped loaf is the next best choice, but steer clear of sandwich loaves, which can’t be cut as easily into the necessary grid pattern.

Set cranberry Brie pull-apart bread out as a party appetizer next to a crudite platter, cocktail meatballs, and a selection of festive cocktails and mocktails. You can also add it to the holiday table as part of the main course, alongside a holiday ham, roast turkey or standing rib roast.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that our classic pecan pie recipe has no chocolate chips, no booze, and no hard-to-find ingredients. Instead of focusing on embellishments, we focused on what matters most: the deep flavor of toasted pecans, a caramelly custard, and a buttery, flaky pie crust.

Brown sugar and a spoonful of dark molasses add depth to the filling, while toasting the pecans before incorporating them makes their flavor stand out and their texture more robust. Blind baking the crust—baking it before adding the filling—helps keep the bottom crisp beneath the gooey custard.

Industry observers note that when the pie comes out of the oven, the edges should be set and slightly puffed, but the center should still wobble like Jell-O. It will continue to set as it cools, so resist slicing too soon. Serve it all on its own, or gild it with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream.

Can I make this pecan pie without corn syrup?

Yes. Corn syrup gives this classic pie its perfectly gooey texture, but there are alternatives. Brown rice syrup will add a toasty flavor and can be used in equal parts. Golden syrup, honey, and maple syrup are all too sweet and will change the pie’s flavor and texture.

For a pie developed without any syrup, try our Bourbon-Date Pecan Pie.

Can I use chopped pecans instead of halves?

Yes. We love the crunch you get from pecan halves, but if you’re a chopped pecan person, use about 225 g in place of the 2 cups of halves. Watch closely when toasting; chopped pecans will need less time in the oven.

Can I make pecan pie ahead of time?

Yes—bake the pie a day ahead and refrigerate it. Let it cool on a rack for up to 2 hours, then transfer it to the refrigerator to finish cooling before covering. To get a head start on the pastry, refrigerate the dough for up to 3 days or freeze it for up to 2 months.

In a recent development, pulse 1 Tbsp. sugar, 1½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and 2 cups all-purpose flour in a food processor until combined. Add 5 Tbsp. chilled unsalted butter, cut into pieces, and 3 Tbsp. chilled lard or vegetable shortening and pulse until mixture resembles coarse meal with a few pieces of butter and lard visible, about fifteen 1-second pulses. With motor running, drizzle in 1 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar and 5½ Tbsp. ice water and pulse until dough is still crumbly but just holds together when squeezed (add 1 tsp. water at a time if necessary, but be careful not to overwork dough).

Turn out dough onto a work surface. Knead 1–2 times, pressing just to incorporate any shaggy pieces. Flatten into a 6"-wide disk. Wrap with plastic wrap and chill at least 1 hour.

Preheat oven to 425°. Roll out dough on a lightly floured work surface to a 14" round. Transfer to a 9" pie pan. Pick up edges and allow dough to slump down into dish, letting excess dough hang over dish. Trim, leaving about a 1" overhang. Fold overhang under; pinch and crimp. Chill 30 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that line dough with parchment paper or foil, leaving some overhang. Fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake until crust is dry around the edges and just beginning to lightly brown, 25–35 minutes. Carefully remove parchment and weights and reduce oven temperature to 350°. Bake until crust is set and beginning to brown in the center, 10–15 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack and let cool.

Sources indicate that do Ahead: Dough can be made 3 days ahead; keep chilled, or freeze up to 2 months. Crust can be baked 1 day ahead; tightly wrap and store at room temperature.

Preheat oven to 350°. Toast 2 cups (225 g) pecan halves on a rimmed baking sheet until browned and fragrant, 8–10 minutes. Let cool.

Reduce oven temperature to 325°. Whisk 4 large eggs, room temperature, beaten to blend, 1 cup light corn syrup, ⅔ cup (packed; 134 g) light brown sugar, 1 Tbsp. robust-flavored (dark) molasses, 1 Tbsp. vanilla extract, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a large bowl until smooth. Slowly whisk in 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter, melted, slightly cooled, until combined. Fold in pecans and pour into cooled crust.

Bake pie until edges are set and slightly puffed but center is recessed and wobbles like Jell-O, 55–70 minutes (it will continue to set after baking). Transfer to a wire rack and let cool at least 3 hours before slicing. Serve with vanilla ice cream.

Do Ahead: Pie can be baked 1 day ahead; tightly wrap and chill. Serve warm or at room temperature.

Recipe by Margaret Knoebel, Milwaukee, Wisconsin.

Tested by Taste of Home Test Kitchen.

Taste of Home's Editorial Process.

Puppy chow is our favorite Midwestern snack, and it’s the inspiration these holiday-ready truffles. You’ll find all the same ingredients—peanut butter, Chex, chocolate and confectioners’ sugar—but with a truffle redesign that’s sophisticated enough for a Christmas dessert table (and that keeps hands considerably less messy!).

In a recent development, like puppy chow, Chex cereal (crushed for easier rolling) and peanut butter are melted together to make the crunchy truffle filling. Each truffle is enrobed in a thick layer of melted chocolate then coated generously with confectioners’ sugar. These puppy chow truffles are a two- to three-bite affair and totally remind me of those massive puppy chow clusters everyone fights over.

Industry observers note that in a large microwave-safe bowl, heat the peanut butter in 30-second increments until it’s completely melted, stirring occasionally. Add 2 tablespoons of confectioners’ sugar and stir until smooth. Add the crushed Chex and stir until everything is well combined.

Sources indicate that scoop the puppy chow truffles by the tablespoonful onto wax-paper-lined baking sheets. Freeze them until they’re firm, about 30 minutes.

In a microwave-safe bowl, melt the semisweet chocolate and shortening at 50% power, and stir until they’re smooth. Dip each puppy chow ball into the melted chocolate and shake off the excess. Place the puppy chow truffles on a waxed paper–lined baking sheet.

Place the confectioners’ sugar in a large airtight container or resealable bag. In batches, add the puppy chow balls and shake them in the bag until they’re well coated in confectioners’ sugar. Store the puppy chow truffles in an airtight container.

Ellie Crowley For Taste Of Home.

Store puppy chow truffles in an airtight container at room temperature for up to four days. They can also last in the fridge for up to one week.

It has been revealed that yes, you can freeze puppy chow truffles, but wait to coat them with confectioners’ sugar until after they’ve thawed. To freeze the puppy chow truffles, place them on a parchment-lined baking sheet and freeze them for one hour. Transfer them to a zip-top bag or airtight container, and freeze them for up to two months. Thaw them overnight in the fridge before enjoying them.

Ellie Crowley For Taste Of Home.

Recent findings suggest that your chocolate may not be smooth for a few reasons. The first is you may have burned it in the microwave. When you burn chocolate, it will seize and become clumpy. Unfortunately, this is unfixable. It’s also possible that you left out the shortening. Shortening makes the chocolate slightly less viscous, which makes it easier to evenly coat the truffles. It also makes it smooth and glossy. Don’t skip this ingredient!

To help puppy chow balls hold their shape, be sure to use a no-stir creamy peanut butter. It’s much thicker than the natural peanut butters you have to stir. Because their oils separate so easily, natural peanut butters will make the mixture softer and more malleable.

Wendy’s is getting nostalgic this holiday season, and as someone who grew up eating in one of the chain’s iconic glass sunrooms, I’m particularly excited about this one.

Industry observers note that the fast food chain just launched a limited-time Holiday Box complete with retro packaging, collectible knit hats, and a choice of some familiar menu favorites. And of course, two fresh peppermint-inspired Frosty desserts.

Obviously, I had to try everything for myself.

Available beginning November 16 at participating Wendy’s locations nationwide, the Holiday Box starts at $11.99 and includes your choice of a Dave’s Double or 10-piece crispy or spicy chicken nuggets, small fries, a small soft drink, and one collectible knit hat.

The packaging is designed to resemble Wendy’s old-school Solarium restaurants, complete with the recognizable glass-walled dining area that became a staple of the chain beginning in the 1980s.

And I have to admit, this one hit me right in the childhood memories.

Sources indicate that growing up, I remember going to Wendy’s with my mom and sitting in that yellow, glass-enclosed sunroom. Seeing the design recreated as a miniature holiday box immediately brought me back to those visits.

Each Holiday Box includes one of four collectible knit hats featuring a retro Wendy’s design: Frosty, Biggie, the classic Wendy’s logo, or the famous “Where’s the Beef?” slogan.

The hats come in sealed mystery bags, meaning you won’t know which one you’re getting until you open it.

Thankfully, I ended up with the blue Frosty beanie, which was exactly the design I was hoping for.

Had I opened the bag to find a hat with “Biggie” written across my forehead, though, I think we would’ve had a problem.

The Holiday Box is available for a limited time while supplies last, and customers can’t select which hat they receive.

Alongside the Holiday Box, Wendy’s is introducing two limited-time desserts: the Peppermint Frosty Swirl and Peppermint Brownie Frosty Fusion.

Both are available with either a vanilla or chocolate Frosty base, so I decided to try one of each.

This was easily my favorite of the two.

The Peppermint Brownie Frosty Fusion combines Wendy’s classic Frosty with peppermint sauce and brownie pieces, creating a dessert that feels especially appropriate for the holiday season.

I went with the vanilla base, and I absolutely loved it.

According to recent reports, the peppermint flavor was strong and immediately reminded me of a candy cane or a York Peppermint Pattie. It had that recognizable minty sweetness I look for in a holiday dessert, without getting lost in the vanilla Frosty.

It has been revealed that the brownie pieces were another highlight, adding a nice texture and a layer of chocolate flavor to the mix. I particularly liked how the chocolate complemented the peppermint rather than competing with it.

Industry observers note that for me, this is exactly what a seasonal Frosty should taste like. It’s festive, flavorful, and different enough from the regular menu to make it worth trying.

For my second dessert, I went with the chocolate Peppermint Frosty Swirl, which combines Wendy’s classic Chocolate Frosty with peppermint sauce.

My biggest piece of advice is to give this one a good stir before digging in.

According to recent reports, when I first tried it, most of the peppermint syrup was concentrated toward the top of the dessert. Mixing everything together helped distribute the flavor more evenly throughout the Frosty.

Once I did that, I really enjoyed it.

The combination of chocolate and peppermint works well, although I didn’t find the mint flavor nearly as strong as it was in the vanilla Brownie Frosty Fusion.

Still, I’m happy to report that Wendy’s peppermint sauce works with both Frosty flavors. If you prefer a more straightforward chocolate-mint combination without brownie pieces, this is a solid option.

Personally, though, I’d go back for the Fusion.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Charles Dickens’s A Christmas Carol occupies a particularly crucial place in my heart.
  • And although I’m generally suspicious of film adaptations of the books I love, there are two versions I treasure every bit as much as the original story.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Taste of Home's Editorial Process.

In a recent development, I'll give you Mr. Scrooge, the Founder of the Feast! Here are all the foods Charles Dickens wrote about in A Christmas Carol.

Charles Dickens’s A Christmas Carol occupies a particularly crucial place in my heart. My grandma gifted me her copy when I was in junior high, and I’ve returned to it nearly every Christmas since, each year finding something in the story that speaks to me in a new way.

And although I’m generally suspicious of film adaptations of the books I love, there are two versions I treasure every bit as much as the original story. I fell in love with them as a child, probably around the same time. The first was The Muppet Christmas Carol, which combined two of my favorite things: the Muppets and jaunty show tunes. I watched it incessantly throughout the Christmas season, and the tradition has carried on with my own children, who now know every song and every word of dialogue.

The other was the 1984 adaptation starring George C. Scott. I love its surreal, slightly unsettling atmosphere, the magnificent strangeness of the Ghost of Christmas Present and the genuinely frightening revelation of Ignorance and Want. And after all that darkness, Scrooge’s redemption is almost unbearably moving.

According to recent reports, with another film adaptation arriving this year (Ebenezer), it’s clear that Dickens’s masterpiece has kept its hold on us. And because the food is an enormous part of what makes the story’s celebrations so memorable, I wanted to take a closer look at the happy commotion of the Cratchits’ kitchen, Fezziwig’s Christmas party and the astonishing abundance surrounding the Ghost of Christmas Present. Nearly two centuries later, those descriptions still give us a remarkably complete picture of what Christmas tasted like in Dickens’s world.

The Cratchits’ Christmas goose is one of the most eagerly anticipated meals in literature. As the family busies itself with the accompaniments, the younger children can hardly contain their excitement. When Mrs. Cratchit finally brings the bird to the table, Dickens describes it arriving with a great flourish and the stuffing spilling out as it’s carved.

It has been revealed that goose was a traditional Christmas centerpiece in Victorian England, particularly for families who couldn’t afford a turkey. Its rich, dark meat was well-suited to roasting, and sage-and-onion stuffing was a familiar accompaniment.

Industry observers note that bob declares that no goose has ever been so tender and delicious, and the family agrees wholeheartedly. The bird may be small for so many people, but the family’s excitement is anything but.

Industry observers note that while the goose roasts, the Cratchit household is busy! Peter tends to the mashed potatoes, Belinda sweetens the apple sauce, and Mrs. Cratchit prepares the gravy. Nearly two centuries later, the menu would look perfectly at home on a modern Christmas table.

According to recent reports, apple sauce was an especially good companion to roast goose, with its tart sweetness balancing the bird’s rich, fatty meat. The mashed potatoes and gravy rounded out the meal, providing plenty of comfort alongside the centerpiece.

For all his considerable literary talents, Charles Dickens also had a good understanding of the anxiety that comes with serving a dessert you’re not entirely sure has turned out.

Industry observers note that while Mrs. Cratchit retrieves her Christmas plum pudding from the kitchen, the family imagines every possible disaster. Perhaps it isn’t cooked through, or perhaps it will break when she turns it out. The younger children even worry that someone might have stolen it. Fortunately, Mrs. Cratchit returns triumphant with a pudding Dickens describes as a “speckled cannon-ball,” blazing with brandy and decorated with holly.

Recent findings suggest that traditionally, plum pudding was a dense mixture of dried fruit, suet, spices and other ingredients, boiled for hours in a cloth. Despite the name, it didn’t necessarily contain plums; the term was historically used for dried fruits such as raisins.

Bob declares the pudding Mrs. Cratchit’s greatest success since their marriage, and nobody dreams of disagreeing. The pudding may be modest in size, but to the Cratchits, it’s a triumph, and Mrs. Cratchit deserves every word of their praise.

According to recent reports, few characters in A Christmas Carol embody the spirit of Christmas quite like old Mr. Fezziwig. When the Ghost of Christmas Past takes Scrooge back to the Christmas party hosted by his former employer, we’re treated to a lively evening of dancing, music, laughter and an impressive assortment of refreshments, including mince pies.

Recent findings suggest that these little pastries had been associated with English Christmas celebrations for generations. Earlier versions of mincemeat often contained actual meat alongside dried fruit, suet and spices. By Dickens’s time, sweeter fillings were increasingly common, though meat hadn’t disappeared from every recipe.

In a recent development, I rather like imagining Fezziwig presiding over the festivities, dispensing good cheer as generously as the food. His party is one of the few memories that briefly softens Scrooge, and it’s easy to understand why.

After the Cratchit family finishes dinner, apples and oranges are brought out, chestnuts are placed on the fire, and Bob serves a warm drink of gin and lemon. With the excitement of the goose and Christmas pudding behind them, the family settles in for the evening.

It has been revealed that roasted chestnuts were a familiar winter treat in Victorian London, sold hot by street vendors and enjoyed at home. Oranges were especially welcome during the winter months, when fresh fruit was less readily available.

In a recent development, dickens mentions that the family has only two tumblers and a custard cup without a handle, a detail I love for its specificity. The bustle of dinner has given way to the quieter pleasure of sitting together, and Dickens allows us to linger with the family a little longer before the evening draws to a close.

Christmas celebrations in Dickens’s England didn’t necessarily end on Dec. 25. Twelfth Night, traditionally observed on Jan. 5 or 6, marked the close of the Twelve Days of Christmas, often with a party and an elaborate cake. Twelfth cakes were rich with dried fruit and spices, beautifully decorated and sometimes baked with a hidden bean. Whoever found the bean in their slice might be crowned king or queen of the festivities, an arrangement that presumably made everyone a little more attentive to their dessert.

In a recent development, dickens details “immense twelfth-cakes” among the extraordinary foods surrounding the Ghost of Christmas Present. The tradition was already evolving by 1843, but the cakes were still familiar enough to belong on his magnificent collection of Christmas indulgences.

Dickens includes entire barrels of oysters among the Ghost of Christmas Present’s holiday foods, which may seem an extravagant addition to modern readers.

Recent findings suggest that in Victorian London, though, oysters were commonly eaten, including by working-class people. They were sold by street vendors, served in taverns and prepared in everything from pies to stews. Britain’s oyster fisheries were once enormously productive, although overharvesting and pollution eventually led to their decline.

Dickens’s Ghost certainly had no shortage of delights surrounding him, but the barrels of oysters wouldn’t necessarily have struck his readers as the most impressive things in the room.

When Scrooge wakes on Christmas morning and realizes he’s been given another chance, one of his first acts is to purchase an enormous turkey for the Cratchits.

He sends a boy to the poulterer’s shop for the prize bird, giddy at the thought of how surprised the family will be. Dickens describes Scrooge’s delight so vividly that it’s difficult not to share his excitement.

Roast turkey was becoming fashionable for Christmas dinner in Victorian England, particularly among wealthier households. Compared with the Cratchits’ modest goose, Scrooge’s gift is a magnificent extravagance.

In a recent development, I especially love that he arranges for the bird to be delivered anonymously. He’s discovered the joy of doing something generous without expecting anything in return, and he can barely contain himself.

According to recent reports, at the end of the story, Scrooge promises Bob Cratchit a raise and suggests they discuss the particulars over a bowl of smoking bishop. It’s a peculiar name for what was essentially a warm, spiced wine punch.

It has been revealed that smoking bishop was traditionally prepared with red wine or port, roasted citrus, sugar and spices. The ingredients were warmed together to make a fragrant cocktail similar to modern mulled wine. It belonged to a family of similarly named punches, including smoking cardinal and smoking pope. Victorian drinkers evidently enjoyed a little ecclesiastical creativity with their beverages.

Sources indicate that I love that Dickens saves this particular drink for the end. We’ve seen the Cratchits gather around their modest dinner and the Ghost of Christmas Present preside over a feast of extraordinary abundance. Now Scrooge, who once wanted nothing to do with either, is inviting Bob Cratchit to share a bowl of punch. Of all the wonderful things on Dickens’s Christmas menu, that invitation may be the most satisfying.

BA's Best Orecchiette With Sausage and Broccoli Rabe

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Unlike many iconic Italian recipes, this luxurious union of silky broccoli rabe, chile-flecked sausage, garlic, and curvaceous pasta is a weeknight hero.
  • While orecchiette is the traditional pasta choice, any short pasta will work.
  • This recipe is one of BA’s Best, our vault of the Test Kitchen's definitive takes on iconic dishes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unlike many iconic Italian recipes, this luxurious union of silky broccoli rabe, chile-flecked sausage, garlic, and curvaceous pasta is a weeknight hero. You can make it start to finish, in about 30 minutes. The key to successful execution is to go way beyond blanching when it comes to precooking the broccoli rabe in boiling salted water. For tender rabe that melds seamlessly with pasta and sausage, start by separating the thick stems from the rest of the stalks and giving them a head start before adding the rest. It removes any unpleasant bitterness and also means the rabe will cook into the saucy base of browned sausage and sweated garlic in just minutes.

While orecchiette is the traditional pasta choice, any short pasta will work. Sausage has become a popular addition to the true original Pugliese dish of stewed broccoli rabe with pasta, but a tin of anchovies makes a great substitute for added oomph and intensity.

This recipe is one of BA’s Best, our vault of the Test Kitchen's definitive takes on iconic dishes.

It has been revealed that cut 2 large bunches broccoli rabe, trimmed, in half crosswise to separate thick stalks from thinner stems and florets. Cook thicker stalks in a medium pot of boiling salted water until crisp-tender, about 5 minutes. Add thinner stems and florets and cook until all of the broccoli rabe is tender (the tip of a paring knife should slide through the stalks with little to no resistance), about 3 minutes. Transfer to a rimmed baking sheet with tongs; let sit until cool enough to handle (no need to squeeze out excess water unless dripping wet). Coarsely chop into bite-size pieces.

Meanwhile, cook 1 lb. orecchiette (little ear-shaped pasta) or other short pasta in a second medium pot of boiling salted water until al dente (or use same pot with fresh salted water). Drain, reserving 2 cups pasta cooking liquid.

According to recent reports, heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a medium Dutch oven or other heavy pot over medium-high. Cook 1 lb. hot Italian sausage, casings removed if needed, breaking up with a wooden spoon, until golden brown and nearly cooked through, about 5 minutes. Add 1 head of garlic, cloves separated, peeled, thinly sliced, and remaining 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Cook, breaking up sausage even finer if needed and stirring often, until garlic is golden brown and softened, 3–4 minutes. Add broccoli rabe and cook, stirring occasionally, until very tender and wilted, about 5 minutes.

Add 4 Tbsp. (½ stick) unsalted butter, cut into pieces, pasta, and 1 cup pasta cooking liquid. Cook, stirring often and adding more pasta cooking liquid as needed, until pasta is coated in a clingy sauce. Taste and add some crushed red pepper flakes if desired. Add 1 oz. Parmesan, finely grated (about ½ cup), and stir, adding more pasta cooking liquid a splash at a time as needed to keep sauce smooth and shiny, until incorporated; season with salt.

Divide pasta among shallow bowls and top with more Parmesan.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that people across the country take breakfast very seriously—after all, many believe it's the most notable meal of the day. When you're rushing to work, grabbing something on the go is often the easiest option. And nothing screams breakfast quite like a side of hash browns. When a diner isn't in the cards, a fast food chain can be just the ticket.

I tried hash browns from five different fast food chains to see which one serves up the best during the morning rush. Of the chains I tried, only Dunkin' serves hash browns all day. Everywhere else, you'll need to order during breakfast hours, which vary by location.

This proved to be one of the tougher taste tests I've conducted during my time at Delish. There were truly no terrible options, and some of the differences were pretty small. Here's how they stacked up.

Sources indicate that burger King's hash browns come in a handy carton filled with plenty of small, round crisps. They have a crunchy exterior and, honestly, are perfectly adequate. They're just up against some tough contenders. Of all the spuds I tried, these were the least memorable and had the least flavor, though nothing about them was off-putting.

Taco Bell served the most substantial hash brown on this list—it was quite hefty. The exterior had a nice crispiness, but compared to its competitors, the inside was much mushier, and the whole thing was noticeably greasier. It's not something I could eat a lot of.

Sources indicate that dunkin's hash browns, which are served all day (!), were a bit more divisive in the Delish office. Some people stood ten toes down for the zesty onion flavor, while others (myself included) found it more reminiscent of leftover grease on a stove. That stated, the texture was great, and whether you love them or hate them, these had the boldest flavor and stood out from the rest of the pack.

It has been revealed that like Taco Bell, McDonald's offers a larger hash brown patty than the others on this list. The chain totally nails the crispy outer edges and boasts great potato flavor. You can really tell this is McDonald's because the taste is so similar to the chain's iconic fries. If you like those, you'll love its hash browns. However, because of the patty's size, the middle lost some of the structure and crispiness I was looking for.

In a surprise win, Chick-fil-A's hash browns came out on top. The bite-sized pieces are easy to grab on the go, and their small size gives each one the perfect mix of a crispy exterior and soft interior. The flavor is spot-on, with savory onion and pepper notes. Best of all, they weren't overly greasy.

“Little Lainey would be losin’ her mind if she knew she was about to be hosting the 60th Annual CMA Awards,” Lainey Wilson mentioned ahead of country music’s biggest night at Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena. Indeed, when Vogue caught up with the chart-topper in a quiet moment leading up to the show, she was incredulous about landing the gig.

According to recent reports, “I’m still that little girl from a town of 200 people in Louisiana who just grew up dreamin’ about being a small part of this world of country music,” Wilson stated in her signature twang. The feeling of going from the middle of nowhere to the center of the ceremony, and in such a milestone year, is nothing short of surreal, she added. Not only was it the show’s six-decade anniversary and a mega year for the genre, but the night was also set to include a tribute to the late Dolly Parton—and the first CMA performance in 13 years from a certain recently wed crossover superstar.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m just excited to celebrate the ones before, the ones now, and the ones comin’,” Wilson noted. “I think the biggest thing for me is being present and being right where my feet are. It’s tryin’ to find that balance.”.

On the day of the show, Downtown Nashville was a flurry of activity, fans, hot chicken, and road closures as the capital of country music prepared to step into the national spotlight. The recent FAA ground stop gave some out-of-towners agita, but the delay clouds thankfully parted in time. Music was ringing out from every bar and restaurant on Broadway, most of the time in the form of Langley’s ubiquitous “Choosin’ Texas.” The country queen of 2026 was also nominated for almost every award imaginable. It’s to the point where if Langley miraculously cloned herself, they’d be nominated for Best Duo, too.

“This isn’t a fad: everyone you know can sing along to every word of ‘Choosin’ Texas,’” Brittany Schaffer, the incoming Country Music Association CEO, told Vogue. Just hours earlier, Schaffer bolted out of her hotel at 6 a.m. to help give out the first award of the day live on Good Morning America. (Naturally, “Choosin’ Texas” won for Best Music Video.) Schaffer was also busy contending with the Taylor of it all, as her CMA comeback was a closely held secret.

Industry observers note that “A small group of us knew for quite a bit of time in advance of the announcement,” Schaffer revealed with a wink. “Obviously, with this being an anniversary, she is such an crucial part of country music history, so we certainly started that conversation with her early on. We are just thrilled that she was so excited to join.”.

In a recent development, while most major red carpets are hectic affairs, the vibe at Music City Center was decidedly chiller—even when an Oscar de la Renta-clad Swift arrived. A hush fell over the space as phones lifted to capture the moment, even that of the lighting technician. Elsewhere, VIPs tucked into fried green tomato sandwiches and sipped whiskey, seemingly unfazed.

“I had to bring my sister, Leslie,” actor Glen Powell, who’s set to play a country music star in next year’s The Comeback King, told Vogue. “ To share this together…I mean, we’ve been country fans our entire lives. We did these long road trips to the ranch, listening to country music the whole way.” A “starstruck” Leslie chimed in: “Two of our childhood idols, Faith Hill and Tim McGraw, are sitting next to us.”.

As the Tennessee sun began to set, a series of Sprinter vans whisked people from the carpet to the arena for a 7 p.m. start time. Backstage, a trophy engraver was waiting to etch the names of future winners into history. Inside the arena, the crowd milled about as a booming voice on the loudspeaker urged, “In respect to Dolly, please take your seats.” It proved to be a subtle teaser, as a tribute featuring Wilson and Vince Gill singing “I Will Always Love You” was about to open the show. Later, Kacey Musgraves and Miranda Lambert lightened the mood with their honky-tonk ode “Horses and Divorces,” from Musgraves’s recent album Middle of Nowhere.

In a recent development, from her dressing room, Musgraves, resplendent in a custom suit by the Los Angeles-based western-wear designer RoseCut, took a breather on the couch. “I think people would be shocked to know how boring my pre-show ritual actually is,” she told Vogue. “It’s pretty chill. I don’t shut myself in a hotel room all day. I try to move and connect with the heartbeat of wherever I’m at.” Alas, a vocal doctor did warn once that she should have “no chocolate, no caffeine, or no booze before a performance. “I’m like, ‘Have you ever been on stage without booze,’” she recalled with a laugh. “So pre-show, the band and I usually do a tequila shot.”.

According to Musgraves, a night like tonight is all about reconnecting. “So many of us here spend so much of our time out on the road. It’s really a reunion of sorts, getting to see a lot of people and friends that you haven’t seen in so long.”.

In a recent development, one of those friends is Megan Moroney, whom Musgraves was happily sharing a dressing room with. Alongside excitement over her two nominations at the CMAs, Moroney is buzzing about her two recently declared Grammy nods. “It’s been such a crazy year,” Moroney told Vogue as the ceremony blared on a TV in the background. “On the morning of the nominations, my manager came into my bedroom at like 6:30 a.m. and noted, ‘We need to turn on the Grammy announcement because I just have a good feeling.’ And I was like, ‘Are you insane?!’”.

The show itself played out as expected. Ella Langley cleaned up, making history by winning everything from Entertainer of the Year to Female Vocalist of the Year and Album of the Year, breaking a CMA record for most wins. Even the country stalwarts were impressed. “A highlight for me was hugging Miranda Lambert,” Lady A’s Hillary Scott told Vogue of Langley’s collaborator. “What’s funny is we toured with her and Kenny Chesney twenty years ago, early on in our careers.” Her bandmate, Dave Haywood, added: “Longevity was the goal when we started. So to be here after all of these years is a dream realized for us.”.

Recent findings suggest that as the show wrapped up and fans departed the arena, stars grabbed snacks to munch on as they got ready to head back out on the road—including a lollipop-sucking Michael Bublé. “What I love about country music is this,” he mused to Vogue, “when you take away all of the production, all of the lights, and all of the magic tricks, you are left with good souls.”.
